title: Italian prototype building models for urban scale building performance simulation
access_depth: Full34-page author manuscript available; selected complete methods/conclusion pages inspected
supports: Physical prototypes specify envelope/HVAC by vintage and use in Italian zoneE, with normative residential internal loads and schedules.
limitations: Does not identify demographic users or validate their assignment; prototypes are not household behaviour measurements.

title: Developing an Italian Library of Reference Buildings for Urban Building Energy Modeling (UBEM): Lessons Learnt from the URBEM Project
access_depth: Publisher-indexed full-text sections; direct429; author-institution records corroborate
supports: Italian UBEM reference-building library formalizes harmonized inputs in traceable scorecards and uncertainty labels.
limitations: Library construction/interoperability does not establish independent measured energy accuracy or user-archetype validity.

title: Validation of a Bayesian-based method for defining residential archetypes in urban building energy models
access_depth: Primary publisher abstract, introduction and section snippets returned
locator: Abstract training399/test2263; Overview; CaseStudy low-rise1–4units; Discussion
supports: Uncertain archetype parameters represented by distributions are updated with monthly/annual meters; a separate larger test population is reported.
limitations: Calibration parameters need not identify household behaviour; Cambridge low-rise data do not establish Italian or hourly transfer.

title: A data-driven approach for multi-scale building archetypes development
access_depth: Author-institution abstract and selected indexed manuscript methods; directfetchfailed
supports: Irish archetypes are separately developed and compared at national, city, county and district scales.
limitations: Scale-specific modeled differences are not proof of measured accuracy; national typologies cannot automatically be assigned city representativeness.

title: Domestic electricity use: a high-resolution energy demand model
access_depth: Primary author-institution abstract and bibliographic record
supports: Activity and active occupancy drive stochastic appliance-use simulation at one-minute resolution, compared with recorded electricity from22UKdwellings.
limitations: Electricity-profile statistical evaluation does not establish heating-control timing or Italian demographic assignment accuracy.

title: A high-resolution stochastic model of domestic activity patterns and electricity demand
access_depth: Primary publisher abstract, introduction and section outline
locator: Abstract; Introduction final paragraphs; §3data/§4evaluation identified but not fully inspected
supports: Time-use-trained nonhomogeneous Markov chains generate individual activities/occupancy and appliance electricity; evaluates household and aggregate properties.
limitations: The modeled end-use scope explicitly excludes heating/maintenance electricity; temporal detail is synthetic and not observation of a specific household.

title: Development of occupancy-integrated archetypes: Use of data mining clustering techniques to embed occupant behaviour profiles in archetypes
access_depth: Full32-page primary author manuscript; selected complete methods/results inspected
supports: Time-use-based occupancy profiles are integrated with physical dwelling archetypes; simulated heating control/internal gains are explicit assumptions.
limitations: Presence is mapped to heating availability by assumption, not direct controller measurement; model differences cannot be called observed savings.

title: A high-temporal resolution residential building occupancy model to generate high-temporal resolution heating load profiles of occupancy-integrated archetypes
access_depth: Primary publisher abstract plus author-released model description
supports: Time-use-based stochastic multi-day occupancy-category profiles are supplied for occupancy-integrated archetypes and heating-load simulation.
limitations: Five activity/presence categories differ from the four Italian demographic archetypes; transfer requires data and definition checks, not relabeling.

title: Stochastic simulation of occupant-driven energy use in a bottom-up residential building stock model
access_depth: Primary publisher abstract/introduction/conclusion indexed; laboratory record corroborates
locator: Abstract; Introduction ResStockworkflow and final paragraphs; ConclusionAndFutureWork
supports: Hybrid Markov/event-duration sampling is integrated with ResStock and checked against time-use and measured end-use electricity data.
limitations: USdata and end-use evaluation do not validate Italian heating schedules. Directly counters generic assertion that ResStock only uses fixed occupancy schedules.

title: A novel population-based occupancy modeling approach for district-scale simulations compared to standard-based methods
access_depth: Primary author-institution abstract and citation; ETHPDFindexed but directfailed
locator: Abstract; full primaryETHmanuscript linked in searchlog
supports: Register-based individuals and daily schedules are compared with deterministic/stochastic standard-based occupancy for district energy simulation.
limitations: Important education/nonresidential context; between-model energy deviations are not measured errors or Italian population evidence.

title: Aggregating set-point temperature profiles for archetype-based: simulations of the space heat demand within residential districts
access_depth: Primary author-institution abstract and indexed authorPDF; directjournal/PDFfailed
supports: Compares three ways to aggregate occupant setpoint profiles for847single-family dwellings, considering different thermal responses.
limitations: Comparison is full versus archetype simulation; numerical aggregation error is not independent metered accuracy. Cannot assume mean-input simulation equals mean outputs.

title: Quantifying uncertainty in multi-scale energy analysis of residential archetypes: A stochastic occupancy approach
access_depth: Primary author-institution abstract and publisher highlights; directfullfetchfailed
supports: Probabilistic occupancy models trained on time-use data are applied to Irish residential archetype energy analysis across scales.
limitations: Full methods/holdout independence not inspected; do not import small error percentages or broad geographical applicability from abstract rhetoric.

title: Smart thermostat data-driven U.S. residential occupancy schedules and development of a U.S. residential occupancy schedule simulator
access_depth: Full27-page primary manuscript; selected methods/limitations inspected
supports: Thermostat-derived occupancy status is clustered into typical schedules and used in theROSSgenerator; status is not occupant count.
limitations: PIRline-of-sight/stationary-person limits, absence of ground truth and opt-in thermostat coverage limit proxy interpretation and transfer.

title: How household thermal routines shape UK home heating demand patterns
access_depth: Primary fullHTML; methods and limitations inspected
supports: Controller schedules and call-for-heat signals reveal temporal household heating routines and synchronization.
limitations: IN/OUT/ASLEEPsettings need not equal actual presence; calls for heat are not direct energy meters; selected337homes not generalizable UKstock.

title: Computationally efficient upscaling of Markovian occupancy models for urban-level building simulations
supports: Compares originalMarkov,temporalrescaling and multinomial aggregation models by statistical fidelity and runtime at different scales.
limitations: Model-to-model occupancy evaluation does not prove building-energy accuracy; paper explicitly leaves heterogeneity and building/end-use interactions for future work.

title: Simulating occupants' impact on building energy performance at different spatial scales
supports: Simulation compares stochastic,rule-based and schedule approaches for occupancy/lighting/shades across office aggregation scales.
limitations: Annual office-lighting convergence cannot establish household heating/peak convergence or universal scale threshold.

title: A numerical analysis of occupancy profile databases impact on dynamic energy simulation of buildings
access_depth: Primary publisher abstract/highlights plus author-institution bibliographic record; institutional fullPDF fetch403
locator: Publisher Abstract/Highlights; Brighton and Pisa author-institution records; primary paper cited as ARCH2025 reference14
supports: Controlled comparison of six occupancy-profile databases in EnergyPlus across three city climates and nine building uses.
limitations: Abstract-level methodological appraisal; database inputs are bundled. Do not import extreme percentages, claim causal mechanisms, or infer independent measured accuracy.
